defect.locator_note: Callout ^rule-good-faith; no text/ directory is disclosed, and the Leon lake record has only pin-922 and a single matched pin-923 excerpt.
defect.problem: The black-letter rule is only partially verifiable from the disclosed evidence. Leon pin-922 supports the warrant-reliance premise and Leon pin-923 verifies only the first failure situation; no disclosed text or matched pinpoint verifies the quoted phrase "so lacking in indicia of probable cause" or all four Leon situations at 468 U.S. 923.
defect.proposed_fix: Add text/United States v. Leon.txt or matched lake pinpoints for the full 468 U.S. at 923 passage covering all four exceptions, including the bare-bones-affidavit quote and facial-deficiency language; otherwise narrow the rule to the portions actually supported by the disclosed pinpoints and cite Franks, Lo-Ji, and Groh separately.

reasons: Leon pin-922 states the issue as evidence obtained by officers acting in objectively reasonable reliance on a warrant issued by a detached and neutral magistrate but later found unsupported by probable cause, so the general warrant-reliance proposition has partial support.

Calandra pin-348 supports the exclusionary rule as judicial deterrent and not a personal right, and Herring pin-144 supports a culpability/deterrence threshold, giving some support to the rule's rationale.
The disclosed Leon pin-923 quote verifies only the false-affidavit situation; the file set contains no opinion text and no pinpoint quote for the bare-bones phrase or the full four-item list.
residual_risks: The rule may be doctrinally correct, but under the disclosed-evidence-only rule it cannot stand at this breadth without the missing Leon 923 text or matched pinpoints.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split the callout into separately supported sentences: Calandra/Herring for deterrence rationale, Leon 922 for warrant reliance, and fully disclosed Leon 923 text plus Franks/Lo-Ji/Groh for the failure floors.
